binders: For every function q: R→R→R, with the first argument denoted x and the second denoted t.
For every real number speed, serving as the scalar coefficient.
For every x∈R and t∈R, specifying the point at which the two slice derivatives are considered.
On the left side, there exist qt∈(Fin 1→R) and then qx∈(Fin 1→R). These witnesses are scoped inside the left proposition and may depend on q, speed, x, and t; qx is quantified within the scope of qt.
On the right side, there exist qt∈R and then qx∈R. These are separate witnesses scoped inside the right proposition and may depend on q, speed, x, and t; qx is quantified within the scope of qt.
The vector dimension is fixed at 1, not universally quantified in the target. The general codomain E of LocalDef006 is instantiated as R.
hypotheses: There are no additional hypotheses on q, speed, x, or t.
Derivative existence is part of each side of the equivalence, rather than an antecedent assumed for all q.
conclusions: Let Q(x,t)(i)=q(x,t) for i∈Fin 1, and let A(i,j)=speed. The following two propositions are equivalent.

Left proposition: there exist vectors a,b∈(Fin 1→R) such that τ↦Q(x,τ) has derivative a at t, ξ↦Q(ξ,t) has derivative b at x, and a+A*b is the zero vector. All three conditions hold simultaneously for the same a and b.

Right proposition: there exist real numbers α,β such that τ↦q(x,τ) has derivative α at t, ξ↦q(ξ,t) has derivative β at x, and α+speed*β=0. All three conditions hold simultaneously for the same α and β.

Thus the one-component vector equation with coefficient matrix [speed] holds at (x,t), with both slice derivatives existing, if and only if the scalar equation ∂q/∂t(x,t)+speed*∂q/∂x(x,t)=0 holds there with both slice derivatives existing.
mathematical_definitions: Fin 1 consists of the single index 0.
A vector in Fin 1→R is a real-valued function on that singleton, with pointwise addition, zero, scalar multiplication, and the product topology.
The lifted field Q is defined at every pair of real arguments and satisfies Q(x,t)(0)=q(x,t).
The coefficient matrix A is the one-by-one real matrix whose only entry is speed.
For the real scalar codomain, HasDerivAt f d s means the ordinary derivative of f at s exists and equals d, equivalently lim_{h→0,h≠0}(f(s+h)-f(s))/h=d.
For the one-component vector codomain, the derivative is taken using pointwise vector operations and the product topology; its unique coordinate is the corresponding real derivative.
The time slice varies the second argument while fixing x; the space slice varies the first argument while fixing t.
Real scalar multiplication on Real is ordinary real multiplication.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every real-valued function q of two real variables, every real coefficient speed, and every real point (x,t), embedding q as a vector with one component makes the following conditions equivalent: the embedded field has a time-slice derivative and a space-slice derivative at (x,t) whose vector values satisfy a+[speed]b=0; and q has the corresponding real slice derivatives at (x,t) whose values satisfy α+speed*β=0. Each condition includes existence of both derivatives. The assertion is a pointwise equivalence between the one-component matrix formulation and the scalar formulation.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The input function is defined on all real pairs, and differentiation uses unrestricted neighborhoods in R. No interval, half-line, boundary, or one-sided derivative is specified.
